# Una Meredith

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v5 c4 P7](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0007)</sub>
- **Origin:** Maywater  <sub>[v5 c4 P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046)</sub>

## Appearance

Una is a small child with dark-blue, almond-shaped, wistful eyes, a pearl-pure face, and a mouth that often falls open over tiny white teeth. Her dead-black hair is worn in straight braids without any curls or kinks. She often wears shabby clothes, including an old gray tam and skimpy, worn-out garments.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P7](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0007), [v5 c12 P5](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0005), [v5 c18 P5](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0005), [v5 c18 P8](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0008), [v5 c34 P5](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0005)_

## Personality

Una is shy, gentle, and deeply sensitive, especially concerning public opinion and her family's unconventional lifestyle. Though quiet and non-confrontational, she possesses a quiet courage and selfless devotion to those she loves, being willing to endure intense personal distress for her father's happiness. She is reverent, timid around strangers, and longs to learn practical skills so that she can take proper care of her home and family.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P7](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0007), [v5 c5 P3](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0003), [v5 c9 P10](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0010), [v5 c9 P11](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0011), [v5 c17 P23](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0023), [v5 c34 P0](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0000), [v5 c34 P3](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0003), [v5 c34 P34](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0034)_

## History

Una grew up in Maywater before her father was called to minister at Glen St. Mary. After finding the runaway orphan Mary Vance hiding in an old barn, Una helped take care of her and comforted her in the manse garret. Overcoming her extreme shyness, Una went to Miss Cornelia Elliott to beg her to adopt Mary so she would not be sent back to an asylum. Una participated in the house-cleaning incident that inadvertently sparked parish scandal, and later took part in a voluntary fast as part of the siblings' Good-Conduct Club punishment, which resulted in her fainting in church. Terrified by Mary Vance's warnings about stepmothers, Una lived in fear of her father remarrying. However, upon overhearing her father's anguish over his unrequited love for Rosemary West, Una privately visited her mother's wedding gown in a closet for strength, then walked to Rosemary's house to ask her to marry her father. Upon delivering Rosemary's reply to her father, she successfully brought about their reconciliation.
